### Radial nerve → PIN
- Pierces the lateral IMS (intermuscular septum) **7.5 cm above the trochlea** (≈4 fingerbreadths) → between **brachialis and BR** (Orthobullets; Prof Mansour)
  [[FIG: Fig 3.33, 3.34, 3.35 · 3.09

- Head → PIN crossing → **≈4 cm in pronation**, 2.5 cm neutral, 2 cm in supination (right in the field) (Prof Mansour)

MUST-KNOW — 5 compression sites of the PIN (Netter)
- **F**ibrous bands in front of the radiocapitellar joint
- **L**eash of Henry (radial recurrent vessels)
- **E**CRB tendinous edge
- **A**rcade of Frohse (proximal supinator) → tendinous in 87% (Konjengbam 2004)
- **S**upinator distal edge → "**FLEAS**"

| | Radial tunnel syndrome | PIN syndrome |
|---|---|---|
| Symptom | **Pain** 3 cm below the epicondyle | **Finger drop**, wrist extends radially (ECRL intact) |
| EMG | Negative | Positive |

(Prof Mansour; Netter; Nagah p36)

- PIN → always **thicker** than the superficial radial nerve (Prof Mansour)
- Radial tunnel injection (steroid + local) → **temporary PIN palsy** possible → ultrasound-guided only; >50% settle without surgery (Prof Mansour)
- Resisted supination, elbow **straight** → only the supinator works → squeezes the PIN; in flexion the biceps supinates (Prof Mansour)
- Resisted **middle finger** extension → ECRB edge over the PIN → pain 3 cm down = tunnel, on the epicondyle = tennis elbow (Prof Mansour)

| | Pronator syndrome | AIN syndrome | CTS (carpal tunnel syndrome) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Numb | Palm too | None | Fingers, palm spared |
| Weak | Long flexors + thenar | FPL, FDP index → **no "OK" sign** | Thenar |

HIGH YIELD — what is at risk, by region
- Anterolateral portal, front of the radial head → **radial nerve / PIN** → ≈4 mm from the distal anterolateral portal in extension (Field 1994)
- Anteromedial portal → **median** + ulnar nerve → stay in front of the medial IMS

- Supracondylar fracture → nerve on the side of the **torn periosteum**: extension → **AIN** (radial if anterolateral); flexion → **ulnar** (Prof Abdel-Ghani)
- **Pucker sign** → spike through brachialis tethers the skin; posteromedial shift → radial nerve, posterolateral → median nerve + brachial artery (TRAUMA sheet)
- Olecranon tension band → K-wire out through the anterior cortex below the coronoid → **AIN** injury, blocked forearm rotation (TRAUMA sheet)
